title: 'The hens suffocated': Fewer, smaller eggs are the double effect of France's scorching summer
subhead: Episodes of extreme heat have exposed stark differences in how well poultry farms are equipped to adapt, with up to 2% of the country's laying hens dying during the June heatwave alone. Beyond excess mortality, the heat also reduces egg production and results in smaller eggs, causing further losses for farmers.

title: Why the song of the summer splintered into a thousand pieces
subhead: As streaming reshapes the music industry, the idea of a single track uniting all generations is giving way to a multitude of hits that are less massive and favored by more targeted audiences.

title: 'Citizens no longer trusted us': Belgium's attempt to revive democracy
subhead: 'Room for Hope' (1/6). High voter abstention, unfulfilled political promises and the growing influence of authoritarian movements have weakened democracies. In response to this crisis, Belgian writer David Van Reybrouck is behind numerous initiatives that hope to reinvigorate democratic practice.

title: Unprecedented crisis grips US colleges, squeezed by soaring costs and Trump-fuelled distrust
subhead: Around 15 higher education institutions closed in 2025 due to debt, and about 40 closed in 2024. In addition to cuts in government funding, academia faced a decline in enrollment as many young people questioned the value of the skills taught.

title: 'What will we have left if we stop loving summer?': Heatwaves crush France's season of insouciance
subhead: The heatwave continues across France, with nearly the entire country under an orange alert on Thursday.
